business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Dehydrated Garlic Flakes and Crushed Chili Pepper Export

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and Regulations; Corporate Transparency Act (CTA) for beneficial ownership reporting to government; Alberta Partnership Act for limited partnership governance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct portal verification; no Apostille required for domestic documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, and key personnel against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, Canadian Sanctions List, and FINTRAC AML/CFT guidelines

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry via Service Alberta
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English language; names must comply with Alberta Business Corporations Act naming conventions
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Trust Company', 'Credit Union' without prior ministerial approval; misleading terms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit administrative appeal to Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of rejection notice, providing evidence of name uniqueness and public interest

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted; virtual offices permissible for registered office address
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; Alberta maintains low risk of unannounced physical inspections for standard LP formations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal services for due diligence and incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Alberta limited partnership formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and consular legalization (for foreign documents)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, ss 50-61 (Limited Partnerships) and Business Names Registration Act, RSA 2000, c B-7, s 12
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Corporate Registry Services)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Partnership (Form LP-1) under Alberta Partnership Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital contributions are governed by the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be cash or in-kind, with the General Partner holding at least one general partnership interest
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The General Partner subscribes to a 1% general partnership interest on behalf of the Limited Partnership and hereby admits the named Limited Partners, whose capital contributions are recorded in the Partnership Register. (2) The registered office of the Limited Partnership is established at [address], Alberta, and the Registration Agent is authorized to file all statutory submissions. (3) [Name] is appointed Chief Administrative Officer and [Name] is appointed Senior Compliance Officer, each with authority to execute banking mandates and export documentation. (4) The Declaration of Partnership be filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry and all fees be paid from partnership funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized NUANS service provider (Service Alberta online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed limited partnership name for a NUANS preliminary search to confirm distinctiveness and availability in Alberta. Where a reserved name is desired, file a Name Reservation Request and pay the applicable fee; a wildcard or alternate name may be noted on the request. Provide a signed consent from the proposed General Partner agreeing to the use of the name.
required_dossiers: NUANS preliminary search report
Name reservation application (Form NR-1)
Proposed partnership name and alternate names
Written consent of General Partner to use proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as confusing, file a revised NUANS search with an alternate distinctive name or obtain a letter of authorization from the prior holder; resubmit within the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of Declaration of Partnership (Form LP-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Registry Services, Edmonton or Calgary office / online filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form LP-1 setting out the limited partnership name, registered address in Alberta, general partner particulars, and the nature of business (wholesale trade in dehydrated vegetables and spices). Ensure the General Partner and every Limited Partner subscribe in writing; file the Declaration electronically or in person at the Corporate Registry, paying the mandatory filing fee. Expedited filing is available for a supplementary fee.
required_dossiers: Completed and executed Form LP-1 (Declaration of Partnership)
Consent to act as registered office provider
Limited Partnership Agreement (executed, kept at registered office)
Authorization from General Partner for filing agent
Filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Declaration is queried for omissions or inconsistent data, file a Correction or Amendment using Form LP-4 with the Corporate Registry within 30 days; in case of rejected filing, correct deficiencies and re-file the Declaration with a new signature date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and CRA Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Alberta Declaration is registered, apply for a federal Business Number (BN) and register for GST/HST, import/export account, and payroll account. Complete Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or submit electronically through the CRA Business Registration Online service, identifying the partnership as a pass-through entity and providing the Alberta LP registration number.
required_dossiers: Alberta Declaration of Partnership registration certificate
Form RC1 - Request for a Business Number
NAICS 424490 activity description
General Partner identification documents
Proposed GST/HST effective date and reporting period
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is rejected or incomplete, call CRA Business Inquiries to rectify omitted fields or amend the account; resubmit Form RC1 with corrected information and supporting partnership records within 5 business days of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Facility Health/Zoning Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable Alberta municipality (e.g. City of Calgary or City of Edmonton) - Licensing Services and Alberta Health Services (AHS) Environmental Public Health
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the municipal business licensing authority for a general wholesale trade business licence in the municipality of the registered office. Where repacking, storing, or handling dehydrated food products is contemplated, register the facility as a food establishment with AHS Environmental Public Health, submitting a floor plan and sanitation schedule. Obtain zoning confirmation that the premises permits wholesale and storage use.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application form
Copy of the Alberta Declaration of Partnership
Lease or proof of premises occupancy
AHS food establishment registration application
Facility floor plan and sanitation procedures
Zoning confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused or conditioned, submit a written application for variance to the municipal development officer or subdivision and development appeal board; for AHS refusal, correct the sanitation deficiencies and request re-inspection or appeal the decision to the Provincial Appeals Board for Health Services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Workers' Compensation and Occupational Health Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Workers' Compensation Board - Alberta (WCB-Alberta) and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership as an employer with WCB-Alberta if any workers, including salaried partners or administrative staff, are engaged. File the WCB Account Registration form and obtain an employer account number. Assess the workplace for OHS compliance, including WHMIS and ergonomic requirements relevant to a warehouse trading operation; retain the OHS hazard assessment at the registered office.
required_dossiers: WCB-Alberta account registration form
Estimated annual payroll declaration
General Partner identification and business contact details
Workplace hazard assessment summary
OHS policy statement (if 5 or more workers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WCB registration is queried, provide revised payroll estimates and legal entity confirmation; for OHS inspection deficiencies, issue a corrective action plan and submit it to the WCB-Alberta claims and assessment division within the compliance deadline stated in the notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Health Services - Environmental Public Health (Safe Healthy Environments) and Alberta Agriculture and Irrigation (Food Safety and Inspection Branch)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Food Establishment Registration (Wholesale / Storage) Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (Alberta EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category B Screening) - Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report not mandated for wholesale storage and trading of dehydrated spices; registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 is triggered only where an industrial wastewater discharge or solid waste threshold is exceeded
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limited to municipal sewer bylaw limits (e.g. City of Calgary Water and Sewer Bylaw: pH 6.0-9.0, BOD <= 300 mg/L, TSS <= 350 mg/L); volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions negligible for dry commodity storage and must remain below the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives; organic spice dust and spent product must be disposed of via approved solid waste facility in accordance with the Recycling Regulation (Alberta Regulation 79/2009)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal fire marshal following annual inspection (fire extinguishers, exit signage, emergency lighting); structural load clearance confirming the warehouse floor and racking systems comply with the National Building Code - Alberta Edition; Alberta OHS workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 and OHS Code, including a signed hazard assessment, first aid equipment, and WHMIS training records for handling bulk spice containers

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada - federal tax administration portal: My Business Account and Business Registration Online at canada.ca/revenue-agency. Customs counterpart: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) CARM/Assessment and Revenue Management portal. Provincial counterpart: Service Alberta / Alberta Corporate Registry (limited partnership registration); Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under a Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement, and Alberta levies no provincial sales tax or separate VAT, so no additional provincial indirect-tax registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Alberta limited partnership: (1) file the initial limited partnership declaration under the Alberta Partnership Act (RSA 2000 c. P-3, Part 2) with the Alberta Corporate Registry / Service Alberta to obtain the Alberta Corporate Access Number; (2) after partnership registration, apply to the CRA via Business Registration Online, or for a non-resident partnership with no Canadian-resident partner or administrator, file Form RC148 'Application for Registration for Non-Resident Businesses', to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN); the application must list all partners with their foreign tax identification numbers and provide a Canadian address for service or an authorized representative; CRA may require security from a non-resident registrant under ETA s. 241; (3) open program accounts on the BN: RT (GST/HST) - mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter plus the four preceding quarters, and recommended for a pure exporter to claim input tax credits; RM (import/export) for customs transactions, and RC for payroll if staff are hired; (4) no separate Alberta corporate TIN or provincial sales-tax account is issued; Alberta corporate income tax is reported on the federal T2 return with AT1 provincial schedules; (5) because the LP is a flow-through, each partner must also obtain a CRA BN or SIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. Under Income Tax Act s. 96 the Alberta limited partnership is not a taxable entity; income, losses, and tax credits flow through to the partners, and non-resident partners are taxed under Part I on their share of Canadian-source partnership business income (with Part XIII withholding applicable only to non-resident allocations paid or credited to the partnership income of a non-resident). For GST/HST, the LP itself is a 'person' and the registrant under the Excise Tax Act. Alberta is a non-participating province, so only the 5% federal GST applies; the LP is eligible for partnership elections and flow-through treatment, and is outside any tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; flow-through status is statutory. Available elections include: (1) ITA s. 97(2) election to transfer property to the partnership at tax cost on formation; (2) partnership fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1(4) to use a non-calendar year end; (3) ETA s. 156 election (Form GST25) to treat certain supplies between closely related corporations/partnerships as not being a supply for GST/HST; (4) ETA quick-method election (Form GST74) for small registrants; and (5) hybrid-mismatch and EIFEL interest-limitation rules (enacted 2022) which can disallow deductions on double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes involving hybrid entities - there is no elective opt-out, but a US LLC corporate partner should be documented under a Section 97(2)/transfer-pricing-compliant structure to minimize hybrid outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - federal value-added tax; Alberta is a non-participating province, so there is no Harmonized Sales Tax and no provincial sales tax; the applicable regime is therefore the 5% federal GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the Excise Tax Act small-supplier threshold (s. 148), measured on total worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) for the current and preceding four calendar quarters; voluntary registration is permitted below that threshold and is virtually always advisable for a zero-rated exporter because it permits recovery of input tax credits and removes the need to prove the threshold is exceeded month-by-month.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or pre-clearance API for invoices. All GST/HST registrants must issue ordinary tax invoices or simplified invoices showing the supplier BN, name, and address; no government validation is required. However, registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 1.5 million must file GST/HST returns electronically and remit by EFT. In the customs corridor, Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) operates mandatory electronic gateways: the eManifest portal for carrier cargo reporting and the CARM system for customs accounting; Canada Export Reporting System (CERS) is used for B13A export declarations where required, though bulk dehydrated garlic and crushed chili pepper (ISIC 4638 / NAICS 424490) are non-controlled commodity exports and ordinarily require no affirmative export declaration apart from carrier eManifest data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI Part I (s. 1), the LP may zero-rate the exported dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper where: (1) the buyer is a non-resident; (2) possession is transferred to the buyer, carrier, or freight forwarder in Canada and the goods are shipped directly to a destination outside Canada; (3) export occurs as soon as a reasonable time after the sale (CRA administrative guidance generally accepts up to one year, with 180 days as the recommended internal benchmark); (4) the LP holds contemporaneous proof-of-export documentation; and (5) the supply is not caught by any exception (e.g., goods leased or licensed for use in Canada, or exported for further processing by a related party under a specified false-export arrangement). Ancillary services performed outside Canada for a non-resident (freight, inspection, storage) are zero-rated as offshore services under Schedule VI Part V. The export invoice must state 'zero-rated' and be excluded from net tax; full input tax credits are claimable on inputs attributable to zero-rated exports. Intercompany export invoices must satisfy ITA s. 247 arm's-length pricing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA/CERS Customs Export Declaration (B13A electronic export report filed only when a declaration is triggered; retained with the export file when filed)
Bill of Lading (ocean, air, rail, or truck) or Cargo Waybill naming the non-resident consignee and showing the outbound port of exit
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 wire log / export letter of credit records showing receipt of funds from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice and sales contract with INCOTERMS (FOB/CIF/CFR foreign port) allocating export responsibility
Carrier or freight forwarder certificate of export plus CBSA marine cargo report (Customs Act s. 12) corroborating physical exit
Certificate of Origin (where an FTA preference is claimed) and CFIA or destination-country phytosanitary/food-safety certificates (where required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit practice for zero-rated exporters requires a complete and contemporaneous documentary chain; absent that evidence, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at 5% GST and the CRA reassesses gross proceeds, with compound daily interest at prescribed rates, plus civil and criminal penalties: (1) gross-negligence penalty of 25% of the net tax under ETA s. 285.1; (2) knowingly false statements or evasion - ETA s. 285 criminal fines and imprisonment; (3) income-tax gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated income under ITA s. 163(2) for related-party mispricing; (4) denial or clawback of input tax credits traced to undocumented export inventory; (5) six-year record-retention duty under ETA s. 286 and ITA s. 230, with penalties for destruction of records; and (6) extended reassessment windows - seven years for misrepresentation, unlimited for fraud. CRA may also audit the exporter's carried-forward ITC pool and recover refunds previously paid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a floating exchange rate regime with full current-account convertibility under the Foreign Exchange Act. Capital-account transactions require voluntary repatriation reporting to the Bank of Canada. Profit remittances to non-resident limited partners are permitted without prior approval, subject only to tax filing and FINTRAC compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Bank of Canada. Receipts must be repatriated and converted to CAD within 90 days or per contractual terms. All export transactions require prior declaration to the Canada Border Services Agency via the Automated Export Reporting System (AERS).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not viable for corporate treasury operations due to strict FINTRAC regulations prohibiting unlicensed money services businesses and restrictions on crypto-asset dealings for Canadian entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Digital remote onboarding is permitted for Alberta Limited Partnerships through bank-approved e-KYC platforms. Physical appearance of directors is not required for standard accounts but may be mandated for accounts exceeding CAD 1 million or involving high-risk jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta corporate registry search results, partnership agreement excerpts, and declarations of beneficial ownership with supporting identification documents

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from source country, export contracts, and proof of legitimate business income
Adverse media reports, PEP declarations, and confirmation of no sanctions exposure

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 wires with purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Accompanying documentation includes partnership agreement, ownership structure, and export sales invoices. All inbound wires require FINTRAC CTR reporting if over CAD 10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements cleared through SWIFT MT103 for commercial payments. Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) issued under UCP 600 rules via correspondent banks. Use of Canadian banks' global networks for settlements in USD, EUR, or other currencies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta; Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of the LP's initial registration, and every anniversary thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may require payment of a late processing fee and blocks issuance of a certificate of status; prolonged default can lead to administrative dissolution of the LP by the Registrar. Restoration generally requires filing all annual returns, paying arrears, and confirming compliance; restricted activity during default may expose general partners to continued liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the calendar year immediately following the partnership's fiscal period end. For a calendar-year fiscal period, the return is due by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA may assess late-filing penalties and T5013 slip penalties under the Income Tax Act; continued non-filing may extend the normal reassessment period for partners and enable CRA compliance enforcement. No administrative strike-off applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit threshold applies to an Alberta limited partnership under the Partnership Act. An audited statement is required only if the partnership agreement mandates it, a financial institution or contractual counterparty requires it, or CRA requests supporting audited financial information during a tax examination. There is no requirement for a private LP to file audited financial statements with the Alberta government.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Alberta Partnership Act does not prescribe IFRS or a specific local GAAP. Partnership accounts must be prepared on a consistent, generally accepted accounting basis that clearly reflects income for Income Tax Act purposes. IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable entities; a private commodity-export LP normally applies Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS consistently as chosen in the partnership agreement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not impose a separate annual public UBO filing on limited partnerships. An LP has partnership interests, not shares; transfers of limited-partner interests are effective under the LP agreement and must be recorded in the register of limited partners. If registered Alberta registry information changes because a partner is admitted, withdrawn, or changes name or address, an Amended Statement must be filed with Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days. Before filing the annual return, the general partner should perform an annual register audit to confirm that the register matches the LP agreement and capital accounts. If the general partner is a corporation, any significant-control-person register obligations under the Alberta Business Corporations Act remain separate.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180–450 per year for an Alberta registered office and registered agent service provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–12,000 per year if an audited statement is required by agreement or a financier; not typically required for a small private LP.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (15% federal + 8% Alberta provincial; levied on corporate partners of the pass-through LP; the limited partnership itself has no separate corporate income tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction for wholesale dehydration/spice trading. Canadian-controlled private corporations may reach 11% combined (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on active business income up to CAD 500,000, but export trading by a non-CCPC or LP-owned corporate partner is generally subject to 23%. Alberta Innovation Employment Grant may provide targeted refundable credits for qualifying R&D/innovation, not passive commodity resale.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (CRA); e-filed via CRA Internet File Transfer or approved commercial software; no corporate T2 is filed by the LP as a taxpayer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the partnership fiscal period-end; e.g., a December 31 year-end LP must file by May 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Partnership name and business number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the exact registered Alberta LP name and the CRA-issued 9-digit business number (BN) with the LP's program account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the LP's Canadian BN; do not substitute a foreign registration number. A non-resident partner list is filed separately in the ownership schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting year-end date used for the partnership; matches the partnership agreement unless a business-purpose change is made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The period must respect the Canadian deemed year-end rules for partnerships with non-resident corporate partners; use the same period in the partner's home-country return to avoid mismatch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List every general and limited partner: name, address, account number, country of tax residence, and percentage sharing ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian tax number/SIN for individuals, Canadian corporate account number or BN for corporations, and foreign tax identification number; attach Form T5013SUM partner allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the LP's gross revenue, deductible expenses, capital cost allowance, and net income/loss; allocate to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement and ITA s.96(1).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be allocated Canadian-source business income attributable to the Alberta permanent establishment; the allocation cannot defer or shift profit for tax avoidance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Exempt income and source codes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify any amounts exempt from partnership income or subject to special source rules (e.g., capital gains, dividend income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, report the character of income at the partner level (business income vs. capital gain) to support treaty classification and foreign tax credit claims.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late/non-filing of T5013: CRA administrative penalty of CAD 100 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); knowingly false statements may attract CAD 100 per day per false statement; general partner remains liable for the LP's compliance and CRA may assess gross-negligence penalties against partners for misallocated income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return (CRA) filed by a corporate partner of the LP; portal: CRA My Business Account / approved EFT software; Alberta corporate income tax is calculated on the same T2 in the applicable provincial schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (instalments are generally quarterly/ monthly for large corporations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the corporate partner's taxation year-end; non-resident corporations with a Canadian permanent establishment via the LP must file and pay Part I tax by the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include the corporate partner's share of LP business income (or loss) for the taxation year, as reported on T5013, in calculating business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner must include the Alberta PE share under Part I; a Part XIII return is not used for this business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply any partnership loss only to the extent of the corporate partner's at-risk amount; reclassify limited partnership loss to Schedule 4 and track carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners with a limited partner interest must respect the at-risk limitation of ITA s.96(2.2) and cannot deduct losses in excess of their contributed capital/loans.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim CCA on depreciable property used in the dehydrated spice business if the partnership has made the appropriate allocation to the corporate partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only depreciable property used in earning Canadian business income qualifies; a non-resident corporate partner may not claim CCA on property used by the LP outside Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total taxable income after applying loss carryovers, charitable donations, and other deductions; this is the base for federal and Alberta corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate federal and Alberta tax only on Canadian PE income; treaty relief, if any, applies only to the corporate partner's residence country and must be separately documented.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; a second late filing within three years raises penalties to 10% plus 2% per month. Interest accrues daily on unpaid amounts; failure to file can also lead to summary conviction under ITA s.238 with fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-resident shareholders. Limited partnership profit allocations/distributions are not dividends and are generally exempt from Part XIII WHT; non-resident partners remain taxable under Part I on allocated Alberta business income. Treaty-reduced dividend rates commonly 5% (≥10% corporate ownership) or 15% (portfolio) under the Canada-US treaty; 10% for qualifying corporate shareholders under the Canada-China DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before the payment date, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) and deliver it to the Canadian withholding agent together with an original Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority for the calendar year of payment. The Canadian payer/LP must retain the NR301, TRC, and supporting ownership/LOB analysis for six years. CRA may request additional substance evidence in a treaty-relief audit; absent valid documentation, the payer must withhold at the statutory 25%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% for both interest and royalties. Arm's-length interest on non-participating debt is commonly exempt under ITA s.212(3). Treaty rates: interest generally 10-15%; IP royalties generally 10% under the Canada-China DTA and other comprehensive DTAs, with 0% for certain copyright/software royalties under the Canada-US Convention. Alberta imposes no additional withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: contemporaneous documentation expected where the taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds CAD 5 million and controlled cross-border transactions exceed CAD 50,000; Master File and Country-by-Country Report at CAD 750 million consolidated group revenue (CRA administrative thresholds; no separate CAD threshold exemption under ITA s.247).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) applicable to Alberta LPs; CRA applies the GAAR in ITA s.245, the sham/substance-over-form doctrine, and treaty limitation-on-benefits/beneficial-ownership analysis. An Alberta LP must have real business activity, Canadian-resident general-partner management, and a valid commercial purpose for exporting dehydrated garlic/chili. Limited partners who participate in management forfeit limited liability; loss deductions are restricted to the at-risk amount under ITA s.96(2.2).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating bulk dehydrated garlic/chili export revenue, inflating supplier costs, concealing foreign bank accounts, or using the LP to invoice personal expenses as business deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s.239: fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax plus imprisonment for up to five years; civil gross-negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2) equal to 50% of the understated tax, plus daily compound interest on unpaid amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/general partners who participated in the evasion may be personally assessed and prosecuted; CRA can impose a court-ordered departure ban under ITA s.179.1 for serious tax debt, freeze personal assets, and obtain seizure orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dehydrated garlic flakes/chili pepper to a related offshore distributor below arm's length, or paying inflated management/royalty fees to a related non-resident company in a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess the LP's income, impose transfer-pricing penalty under ITA s.247(3) equal to 10% of the net adjustment, add interest, and make a consequential adjustment to any related Canadian corporate partner's return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Not automatic, but directors who knowingly sign false T2/T5013 schedules or direct the mispricing may face gross-negligence penalties and criminal liability; treaty APAs/MAP procedures do not waive domestic penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an Alberta registered office and LP agreement only to access treaty benefits, without Canadian employees, storage, or procurement activities in dehydrated spice export; routing invoices through a foreign intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR can disallow the entire tax benefit under ITA s.245; reassessments with interest; CRA may also deny treaty benefits on the ground that the foreign partner is not the beneficial owner; penalty under ITA s.163(2) if the misrepresentation is knowing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A shell LP may be disregarded, exposing the general partner to unlimited liability for partnership debts; directors of a corporate general partner can be held personally liable for CRA withholding and for fraudulent conveyance where assets have been stripped.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mis-invoicing container shipments of dehydrated garlic/chili (over/under-invoicing), receiving rapid TT wire payments from unknown shell customers, or using complex SWIFT LC payment chains inconsistent with wholesale commodity pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC penalties for money-laundering violations under PCMLTFA: up to CAD 1 million per administrative violation for entities; criminal money-laundering under Criminal Code s.462.31 carries imprisonment up to 10 years; proceeds are subject to confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/officers who approve or knowingly implement laundering transactions face personal criminal prosecution, confiscation, and extradition; insurance or corporate indemnity generally will not cover deliberate criminality.
